data.why: sceRNA.csv is read by app.py at startup but is not committed to the repo, so a synthetic scRNA-seq expression table (TP10K-like values, symbol + 9 spermatogenesis stage columns) was written to seed/ at the repo root path app.py expects; gene_list.txt is a matching gene list for the browser to upload, including a flat-expression gene (Actb, std=0) and a gene with a missing value (Ddx4) to exercise the app's dropna/std filtering.

goals: check whether known spermatogenesis marker genes show the expected stage-specific expression pattern
compare raw TP10K expression versus z-score normalized expression across stages for a gene set
identify which genes cluster together in expression dynamics via the hierarchical clustering heatmap
spot genes with flat or missing expression that get silently dropped from the analysis
summarize expression trends (mean, median, quartiles) across a gene list spanning the full spermatogenesis timeline

review.summary: The tree captures this single-form tool well: its phases follow the real analysis arc from giving genes through peak checks, raw vs z-score comparison, clustering and summary to auditing dropped genes, and the cited screens support nearly every claim. It needs fixes before filing: it misses that the uploaded list's Ddx4 and Actb were silently filtered (the very behaviour the data was seeded to show), it misstates the gene-list size and some failure cases, and it doesn't flag that the expression matrix is synthetic.
